title: Coordinate quadratic cotangent multiplication and formal quadratic relations
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative local ring, $k=A/\mathfrak m$, $d\geq0$, and $b=(b_i)_{i\in\{1,\ldots,d\}}$ a $k$-basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$. Quotients and ideal powers use [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient, def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. Write $W_d(k)\subseteq k[X_1,\ldots,X_d]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] for the submodule of homogeneous polynomials of total degree two, and use the standard quotient model $T_2(A)=\mathfrak m^2/(\mathfrak m\cdot\mathfrak m^2)$ of $\mathfrak m^2/\mathfrak m^3$, with its canonical $k$-module structure. For a coefficient section $s:k\to A$ of the residue map and lifts $x_i\in\mathfrak m$ of $b_i$, define $E_{s,x}(q)=\sum_{\alpha\in\operatorname{supp}(q)}s(q_\alpha)\prod_i x_i^{\alpha_i}$. A $k$-linear map $\mu:W_d(k)\to T_2(A)$ is quadratic cotangent multiplication for $b$ if for every such $s,x$ and every $q$, its image under the canonical inclusion $T_2(A)\hookrightarrow A/\mathfrak m^3$ equals $E_{s,x}(q)\bmod\mathfrak m^3$; its quadratic relation space is $\ker\mu$. For commutative rings $k,k'$, a ring homomorphism $\sigma:k\to k'$ and a $d\times d'$ matrix $P$ [def-weil-matrix], define the coefficient-and-linear substitution $T_{\sigma,P}(q)=q^\sigma(\sum_jP_{1j}X'_j,\ldots,\sum_jP_{dj}X'_j)$. For any binary polynomial $q$ over a commutative ring, its binary polar matrix is $B(q)_{ii}=2q_{2e_i}$ and $B(q)_{ij}=q_{e_1+e_2}$ for $i\ne j$. Finally for a field $F$, $e\geq0$, $S=F[[z_1,\ldots,z_e]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], $\mathfrak p=(z_1,\ldots,z_e)$ and any ideal $H\subseteq S$, define the formal quadratic relation kernel as the $F$-submodule $\{q\in W_e(F):q\text{ viewed in }S\text{ belongs to }\mathfrak p^3+H\}$.
